recipes.name: Almond Brownie Cookies
instructions: In a small bowl, combine the flaxseeds and water. Set aside.
Fill a saucepan halfway with water and bring it to a boil. Place a large heat safe bowl over the saucepan. Add the chocolate and coconut oil and stir until melted and smooth.
Add the brown sugar and mix well. Carefully remove the bowl from the heat, as it will be hot.
Stir in the flaxseed mixture, almonds, and vanilla.
Sift in the flour, baking powder, and salt. Stir until just combined, being careful not to overmix. Let the dough rest at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Line a baking tray and preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C)*.

Scoop about 1½ Tbsp of dough per cookie and roll into small balls with your hands. Place them on the baking tray and gently flatten into disks about 1 cm thick (they don't spread much on their own). Leave about 5 cm between each cookie.
To decorate, gently press a few small pieces of chopped chocolate and chopped almonds onto the top of each cookie, if desired. Bake for 10 to 11 minutes.
Once out of the oven, sprinkle with flaky sea salt, if desired. Let cool on the baking tray for a few minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely. Enjoy!

page_recipe_notes: Notes † Tip: best to choose a chocolate that's tasty enough that you'd enjoy eating it on its own. Chocolate is one of the main ingredients in this recipe, so the taste of the final cookies depends largely on the taste of the chocolate used. † Refined coconut oil is coconut oil that doesn't smell or taste like coconuts. If you prefer a distinct coconut taste, use unrefined coconut oil instead. † We've also made this recipe using 1¼ cup (156 g) flour, which yields a more firm, cake-like cookie rather than a soft and brownie-like cookie. Both taste delicious, so you can use whichever measurement you prefer. * We used top and bottom heating (not fan-assisted/convection).
Storage Store in an airtight container on the counter for up to 3 days.
